summary: A widow is fed from the orphans' property, so what she earns belongs to them. Her own heirs, who inherit her kesubah, must pay for her burial.

chunks.en: A widow is fed from the orphans' property.
chunks.st: A widow is sustained from the property of orphans.

chunks.en: What she earns belongs to them,
chunks.st: Her earnings belong to them,

chunks.en: and they do not have to bury her.
chunks.st: and they are not obligated to see to her burial.

chunks.en: Her heirs, who inherit her kesubah,
chunks.st: Her heirs, who inherit her marriage contract,

chunks.en: must pay for her burial.
chunks.st: are obligated to see to her burial.

summary: A widow may sell her late husband's property for her kesubah without beis din. Rabbi Shimon says a widow from erusin, who is not fed from the property, may sell only through beis din.

chunks.he: אַלְמָנָה, בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין,
chunks.en: A widow, whether after erusin or after marriage,
chunks.st: A widow, whether widowed from betrothal or from marriage,

chunks.en: may sell without beis din.
chunks.st: sells her husband’s property when not in court.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: after marriage,
chunks.st: A widow from marriage

chunks.en: she may sell without beis din.
chunks.st: sells when not in court,

chunks.en: After erusin,
chunks.st: but a widow from betrothal

chunks.en: she may sell only through beis din,
chunks.st: may sell only in court,

chunks.en: because she does not get food,
chunks.st: because she does not receive sustenance
chunks.stMore: from her husband’s property. She receives only her marriage contract,

chunks.en: and anyone who does not get food
chunks.st: and anyone who does not receive sustenance

chunks.en: may sell only through beis din.
chunks.st: may sell only in court.

summary: A widow who already sold or gave away part of her kesubah must sell the rest through beis din. The Sages say she may sell many times on her own, and a divorced woman sells only through beis din.

chunks.en: If she sold her kesubah or part of it,
chunks.st: sold all or part of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: if she gave her kesubah or part of it as a pledge,
chunks.st: or if she mortgaged all or part of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: if she gave her kesubah or part of it to someone else,
chunks.st: or if she gave away as a gift all or part of her marriage contract to another,

chunks.en: she may not sell the rest
chunks.st: then she sells the remainder

chunks.en: except through beis din.
chunks.st: only in court.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: מוֹכֶרֶת הִיא אֲפִלּוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה פְעָמִים,
chunks.en: she may sell even four or five times,
chunks.st: She sells even four or five times,
chunks.stMore: and she is not obligated to sell everything at one time.

chunks.en: and she sells for food without beis din,
chunks.st: And despite selling several times, she sells for her sustenance even when not in court,

chunks.en: and she writes, I sold it for food.
chunks.st: and she writes in the bill of sale: I sold this for my sustenance.

chunks.he: וּגְרוּשָׁה לֹא תִמְכֹּר אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין:
chunks.en: And a divorced woman may sell only through beis din.
chunks.st: And a divorcée, who does not receive sustenance, sells only in court.

summary: If a widow sold property for less than it was worth to collect her kesubah, sometimes the sale does not count. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says the sale counts unless the mistake was big.

chunks.he: אַלְמָנָה שֶׁהָיְתָה כְתֻבָּתָהּ מָאתַיִם וּמָכְרָה שָׁוֶה
chunks.en: A widow whose kesubah was two hundred, and she sold something worth
chunks.st: a widow whose marriage contract was worth two hundred dinars and she sold property that was worth

chunks.he: מָנֶה בְמָאתַיִם אוֹ שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם בְּמָנֶה,
chunks.en: one hundred for two hundred, or worth two hundred for one hundred,
chunks.st: one hundred dinars for two hundred dinars, or if she sold property worth two hundred dinars for one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: she has gotten her kesubah.
chunks.st: she has received payment of her marriage contract and can demand nothing more.

chunks.en: If her kesubah was one hundred, and she sold
chunks.st: If her marriage contract was worth one hundred dinars and she sold

chunks.en: something worth one hundred and a dinar for one hundred,
chunks.st: property worth one hundred dinars and a dinar for one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: her sale does not count.
chunks.st: the sale is void
chunks.stMore: because she sold property that did not belong to her.

chunks.en: Even if she says, I will give back
chunks.st: Even if she says: I will return

chunks.en: the dinar to the heirs,
chunks.st: the additional dinar to the heirs,

chunks.en: her sale does not count.
chunks.st: the sale is nevertheless void.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: לְעוֹלָם מִכְרָהּ קַיָּם עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא שָׁם
chunks.en: Her sale always counts, unless there is
chunks.st: Actually, the sale is valid. It is not considered an invalid sale until there is
chunks.stMore: an error so extreme that had there been no mistake,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּשַׁיֵּר בְּשָׂדֶה בַּת תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּים,
chunks.en: enough to leave a field of nine kav,
chunks.st: there would have remained in the field an area required for sowing nine kav of seed,
chunks.stMore: the smallest area of land worth working. In that case, the orphans can reasonably claim that they are unwilling to give up on the land that belongs to them. However, if the error is less than this, it is enough if she returns the remainder to the orphans.

chunks.en: or in a garden, half a kav,
chunks.st: And in the case of a garden, the sale is void if, had there been no error, there would have remained an area required for sowing a half-kav of seed,
chunks.stMore: as this is the smallest size of garden worth working.

chunks.en: or as Rabbi Akiva says, a quarter kav.
chunks.st: Or, according to the statement of Rabbi Akiva, an area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed.

chunks.en: If her kesubah was four hundred zuz,
chunks.st: If her marriage contract was worth four hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and she sold to this one for one hundred, and to that one for one hundred,
chunks.st: and she sold property to this one for one hundred dinars, and she sold property to that one for one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and to the last one something worth one hundred and a dinar for one hundred,
chunks.st: and again to a third one, and she sold property to the last one worth one hundred dinars and a dinar for only one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: the last one's sale does not count, and
chunks.st: the sale of the last property is void, as the price she charged was below the market value. And

chunks.en: all the others, their sale counts.
chunks.st: all of the others, their sale is valid, as they were sold for the correct price.

chunks.en: or a sixth too high,
chunks.st: or added one-sixth to its market value,

chunks.en: their sale does not count.
chunks.st: their sale is void.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

summary: Some women do not get a kesubah because the marriage was not proper. But women married to someone the Torah forbids them to marry still get a kesubah.
stIntro: An orphan girl who was married off by her mother or brother before reaching the age of majority may refuse to continue living with her husband upon reaching the age of majority, thereby retroactively annulling their marriage. In the case of

chunks.en: A girl who refuses, a sheniyah,
chunks.st: one who refuses to continue living with her husband in this manner; and in the case of a woman who is a secondary forbidden relative by rabbinic law;

words.note: A girl married off very young who says no when she grows up.
A relative the Rabbis forbade to marry.

chunks.he: וְהָאַיְלוֹנִית, אֵין לָהֶם כְּתֻבָּה וְלֹא פֵרוֹת,
chunks.en: and an aylonis do not get a kesubah, or payment for fruits,
chunks.st: and in the case of a sexually underdeveloped woman [ailonit], who is incapable of bearing children, each of these women is not entitled to payment of a marriage contract; and they are not entitled to remuneration for the produce that the husband consumed;

words.note: A woman who cannot have children.

chunks.en: or food,
chunks.st: and they are not entitled to sustenance;

chunks.en: or their worn-out clothes.
chunks.st: and they are not entitled to their worn clothes
chunks.stMore: that were brought in to the marriage as part of their dowry and became worn out during the marriage.

chunks.en: But if he married her from the start knowing she is an aylonis,
chunks.st: If, from the start, he married her with the understanding that she is an ailonit,

chunks.en: she gets a kesubah.
chunks.st: then she is entitled to payment of a marriage contract.

chunks.en: A widow married to a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: In the case of a widow who married a High Priest;

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah married to a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: or a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza and later married a common priest;

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah married to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: or a daughter born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzeret] who married an Israelite; or a Gibeonite woman who married an Israelite;

chunks.en: a Jewish girl married to a nasin or a mamzer,
chunks.st: or a Jewish woman who married a Gibeonite or a mamzer,
chunks.stMore: although each of these unions is prohibited by Torah law, the woman is still

chunks.en: they do get a kesubah.
chunks.st: entitled to payment of a marriage contract.
